methods.name: Nonlinear additive noise model
methods.protocol_description: Model: y := f(x) + n, with x and n independent, f nonlinear. Identifiability based on asymmetry: if forward model holds, residuals are independent of cause; reverse model typically yields dependent residuals.

study_units.name: Two-variable identifiability analysis

provenance.text_excerpt: for nonlinear models with additive noise almost any nonlinearities (invertible or not) will typically yield identiﬁable models.

results.value_raw_text: For nonlinear models with additive noise, almost any nonlinearities (invertible or not) will typically yield identifiable models.

provenance.text_excerpt: We test whether a model y := f(x)+n is consistent with the data, simply by doing a nonlinear regression of y on x (to get an estimate ˆf of f), calculating the corresponding residuals ˆn = y −ˆf(x), and testing whether ˆn is independent of x. If so, we accept the model y := f(x) + n; if not, we reject it.

claims.statement: The proposed method can infer causal direction by testing independence of residuals and cause.

experiments_or_tasks: Propose a method to infer causal graph from sample data using nonlinear regression and independence tests.

methods.name: Two-step causal direction test
methods.protocol_description: For two variables x,y: (1) test independence; if dependent, (2) regress y on x, compute residuals, test independence of residuals and x; if independent, accept forward model. Repeat for reverse direction. Generalize to N variables by testing each DAG: regress each variable on parents, test mutual independence of residuals.

provenance.text_excerpt: Panel (a) shows that our method can solve the well-known linear but non-Gaussian special case [7]. By plotting the acceptance probability of the correct and the reverse model as a function of non-Gaussianity we can see that when the distributions are sufﬁciently non-Gaussian the method is able to infer the correct causal direction. Then, in panel (b) we similarly demonstrate that we can identify the correct direction for the Gaussian marginal and Gaussian noise model when the functional relationship is sufﬁciently nonlinear.

results.value_raw_text: When q is sufficiently non-Gaussian, method infers correct direction (panel a). When b is sufficiently nonlinear, method infers correct direction even for Gaussian noise (panel b).

results.value_raw_text: Model is identifiable also for positive b (invertible function), indicating non-invertibility is not necessary.
